text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 4 in history:
1209 - Otto IV was crowned Holy Roman Emperor.
1289 - Louis X (or Le Hutin or the Stubborn), King of France from 1314, born.
1550 - Charles IX of Sweden born. Ruler of Sweden from 1599 and then King from 1607, he carried out an aggressive foreign policy and made war with Poland and Denmark.
1582 - Saint Teresa died. She founded the convent of St. Joseph of Avila and re-established the Carmelite rule in nunneries.

1582 - Today was the last day of the Julian Calendar in the Papal states, Spain and Portugal. Pope Gregory's Gregorian calendar took effect the next day, which became 15 October to allow for the 10-day error which the Julian system had accumulated.
1669 - Rembrandt (Harmenszoon van Rijn) died. Dutch painter of portraits, religious works and landscapes, his combined delicacy and power made him one of history's greatest painters.
1787 - Francois Pierre Guillaume Guizot, French historian and politician who was foreign minister of France from 1840 to 1848, born.
1819 - Italian statesman Francesco Crispi born. Exiled from Naples for revolutionary activities, he later became premier of a united Italy.
1822 - Rutherford Birchard Hayes, 19th president of the United States from 1877 to 1881, born.
1830 - Belgium formed itself into an independent state, having been part of the Netherlands since 1815.
1853 - After Russia refused to withdraw from the Danubian principalities, Turkey declared war thus starting the war in the Crimea.
1878 - The first Chinese embassy opened in the United States when Chen Lan-Pin presented his papers as Envoy-Extraordinary to President Hayes.
1892 - Engelbert Dollfuss, Austrian statesman born.
Chancellor of Austria from 1932 he came into conflict with Hitler's Germany in 1934 and was murdered by Austrian Nazis.

1895 - (Joseph Francis) Buster Keaton born. One of the great comedians of the silent film era who also directed his own films. He appeared from 1917 in films such as "The Navigator" and "The General".
1924 - Charlton Heston (Charles Carter), U.S. film and stage actor, born. Famous for his epic appearances in films such as "El Cid" and "Ben Hur" for which he won an Oscar.
1940 - Adolf Hitler, Mussolini and their foreign ministers held a summit meeting on an armoured train at the Brenner Pass.
1943 - The liberation of Corsica by the Free French forces was completed.
1948 - Sir Arthur Whitten Brown, who made the first non-stop flight across the Atlantic along with John Alcock in 1919, died.
1952 - The first pacemaker to control the body's heartbeat, developed by Dr Paul Zoll of Harvard University, was fitted externally to David Schwartz.
1957 - The Soviet Union became the first nation to go into space when it launched the man-made satellite Sputnik-I into orbit 500 miles above the Earth.
1965 - Pope Paul VI became the first Pope to visit the United States and address the United Nations.
1966 - Lesotho, formerly the British colony of Basutoland, achieved its independence and became a member of the Commonwealth.
1969 - Reuters correspondent Anthony Grey was freed from house arrest after being held by the Chinese for 26 months.
1970 - Janis Joplin, noted blues and soul singer was found dead of a drugs overdose.
1990 - Former Colonel Alexander Noble launched a separatist insurrection in the southern Philippines and took over the cities of Butuan and Caqayan de Oro.
1992 - The Mozambique government and rebel leaders signed a ceasefire to end the 16-year civil war.

1993 - Boris Yeltsin crushed a hardline Communist rebellion. After a 10-hour tank assault on the White House parliament building, sacked vice-president Alexander Rutskoi and other opposition leaders were herded into Lefortovo jail.
